parsed.rationale: Both `WXYCBackground` and `WXYCGradient` are `type-alias-object` records in the same package (`WXUI`) with `shared_field_count: 2` and no differing slots, strongly suggesting they alias the same underlying type. Neither record carries any restraint marker (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the duplication is live production code. Because both are type aliases rather than concrete declarations, the correct resolution is to consolidate to a single canonical alias name rather than extracting, lifting, or genericizing anything. The name `WXYCGradient` is more consistent with the project's WXYC-prefix naming convention visible in the file name `WXYCGradient.swift`, making it the preferred survivor.

specifics.proposed_action: Investigate whether `WXYCBackground` (in `Shared/WXUI/Sources/WXUI/BackgroundGradient.swift`) and `WXYCGradient` (in `Shared/WXUI/Sources/WXUI/WXYCGradient.swift`) are truly aliasing the same underlying type. If so, deprecate one alias (likely `WXYCBackground`, as it is less name-consistent with the WXYC prefix convention) and replace all call sites with the surviving alias `WXYCGradient`. If they alias different underlying types that happen to share the same structural shape, no merge is warranted and the names should be left as-is.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with no fields (`fields_or_signature: []`). Because they are type aliases rather than concrete types, structs, classes, or protocols, none of the standard refactor categories apply cleanly: there is nothing to extract into a shared type, no protocol hierarchy to introduce, no default implementation to provide, and no generic parameterization to perform. The actionable question is purely whether one alias is redundant and should be removed — a rename/deprecation operation that does not map to any of the named categories.
